newsitem.title: USA: No new USDA office closings yet - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: No new USDA office closings yet - Glickman.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, trying to allay fears in farm country, said Friday he had approved no new plans for additional closings of Farm Service Agency offices.
"I have not approved the closure of any FSA offices or any plan to do so," Glickman said in a statement.
The Clinton administration has proposed reducing the number of FSA offices to 1,500, compared to the current target of 2,000 in 1999.
Glickman said nothing would happen unless Congress and the administration agreed on a plan for further streamlining. Talk about potential closings amounted to nothing more than talk, he said.
Glickman made similar statements in a satellite hook-up with corn and soybean farmers at a convention in Florida earlier in the day.
